_comment: The declared required status checks for `main`, and the deliberate exclusions.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Required checks live in GitHub branch protection, which
no one reads and nothing reconciles: a job added to ci.yml is simply never
required until a human remembers. That is not hypothetical — in
be-botresources.ai several e2e jobs sat un-required for months, one of them
from the day it shipped, blocking nothing they were written to block.
So the list is declared HERE, beside the workflow it describes, and
scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh reads its contexts from this array rather
than carrying a second copy of it.
Entries are the job's DISPLAY name (`name:` in ci.yml, falling back to the
job id) — that is the string branch protection matches on.
Bootstrapped by runkit with the jobs ci.yml ships with — the same gate set
the backend monorepo runs, minus what a standalone repository has no use
for. Each service runkit scaffolds adds its own
`e2e <service> (reality chains)` entry beside them, in the same run that
_note_on_skipped_jobs: The per-service e2e jobs are path-filtered by the `changes` job (a job-level
`if:`), and requiring a filtered job is SAFE as long as ci.yml carries no
workflow-level `paths:` filter: the workflow always runs, and a job skipped
by its `if:` still reports a `skipped` conclusion, which satisfies branch
That safety evaporates the day someone adds a workflow-level `paths:` filter
to ci.yml — the check would never report and every PR would hang. Don't.
